reviews.review:
Just to be clear, I absolutely love this game. Warframe is not a [i]bad[/i] game; it's got fun gameplay, plenty of variety in its missions, maps, warframes, weapons, etc., and it's completely free to play (as in you don't need to pay real life money in order to unlock certain content in-game). If you can stand the sheer "grindiness" of Warframe, it can be a pleasant experience. [b]However[/b], at least in my opinion, the game has one main problem that holds it back significantly:


[h1]The grind is merciless to casuals.[/h1]

Well, that might be an exaggeration on my part, but the point I'm trying to get across is that Warframe gets grindy, [i] very [/i] grindy, even during mid-game, to the point that many new players (most of which are casual players) might consider it absurd ([spoiler]Examples include ranking up, some warframes, the Plains of Eidolon (the -lysts specifically), Orb Vallis (the heist), and the Railjack[/spoiler]). This usually marks the "end of the line" for those players, because of the amount of time and dedication needed to achieve most things in Warframe.

Of course, you can use Platinum in-game to reduce the amount of time needed to make weapons/warframes, but many casual players do not buy platinum and obtaining it for free is quite the challenge (not to mention the fact that to a new player, trading items for plat successfully is very difficult, as they have to [u] grind[/u] in order to obtain valuable items to trade with).

The worst part is that solo players are affected the most, because Warframe heavily encourages cooperative play, to the point that sometimes playing alone is ridiculously unfair (especially when trying to fight high-level enemies, even with good weapon/warframe builds). They abandon the game after this point because if they either don't join a clan or make one with only their friends (I personally did this, but I highly encourage people to choose the former option first and only after reaching end-game to make their own clans; grinding for resources is difficult for a clan with few members, most of them new players) their experience with the game will become more and more agonizing, transforming the act of progression into a chore.

In Conclusion, Warframe's grind is not an inherently bad game mechanic; however it can easily drive away casual and solo players, which leads to a decrease in players overall.

The main purpose of this review is to encourage any newcomer to play Warframe, and to form their own opinions about the game in its current state. (after all, I'm one guy on the Internet; don't take anything I say as gospel.)
For a Free-to-Play this game this one is amazing. Credit to the dev's they really listen to their fan base, it shows in the game play and changes that have been made to the game over the years.
If you love grinding this is the game for you!
